relevance_note: Case report of an infant with a heterozygous TNFAIP3 variant and her carrier father and paternal uncle: "We identified a heterozygous variant in TNFAIP3, namely NM_006290.4:c.460G > T".
method_note: Read by hand; JSON assembled with a short Python script whose values were typed from my reading. No tables in the paper. Labels: the proband is the single unnamed case-report patient ('patient'); relatives labelled by relation as written in the family-history sentence. In scope: proband, father and father's brother (both stated to carry the same TNFAIP3 variant), the mother (screened for TNFAIP3; her result is not stated explicitly, only that the TNFAIP3 variant was of paternal origin, so no variant row), and three affected paternal relatives described in the family history (paternal grandfather, brother of paternal grandfather, father's uncle) who were not screened. The paper does not say whether 'father's uncle' and 'brother of paternal grandfather' are the same person; kept as two rows as listed. TNFRSF13B c.204dupA in the proband (maternal origin; mother as carrier) is described as a 'known risk allele' and was left out under the risk-allele rule. Father and uncle variant rows copy the proband's printed variant string, supported by 'the same' variant statements; zygosity, type, inheritance and pathogenicity left not reported for them (stated only for the proband). Proband variant type 'nonsense' from 'resulting in a premature stop codon'. No formal pathogenicity class stated ('not previously described', 'novel'), so pathogenicity left not reported. 'One-year-old' is the age at presentation to the centre, not at last evaluation or diagnosis, so those ages are not reported. Normal first-level autoimmune tests (VES, complement, immunoglobulins, TNF, lymphocyte subpopulations, ASCA, ANCA) recorded as excluded abnormalities, keeping the paper's term 'VES'; 'exams for infectious disease and neoplastic conditions were all negative' and the normal physical examination recorded as the paper words them. Differential diagnoses ruled out (allergic colitis, ADA-2 deficiency, VEO-IBD genetic studies negative) not recorded as features. Inflammatory markers 'negative' after treatment is a later resolution, not recorded as exclusion; checklist kept observed. Fever was a single febrile episode, so 'recurrent fever' not reported. Diabetes was a steroid side effect, so 'type 1 diabetes' not reported. Lymphoid nodular hyperplasia was only 'suggestive' macroscopically; lymphoproliferation checklist not reported. Father's vitiligo not counted under the composite skin-lesions item. No contradictions found.
